items.why_flagged: A_academy audit: unverified.

items.why_flagged: A_academy audit: cite.

items.why_flagged: R9_T2_parent_wasia.

items.where_in_app: The Path (new Muslim) > Established tag
items.what_to_review: [Established] on a thin lesson implies completeness; a card says "pray as you have seen" with no school stated.
items.why_flagged: R9_T3_new_muslim.

items.where_in_app: Hadi chat > choosing which answer to show
items.what_to_review: Which question gets which answer (for example prepaid funeral plan, combining prayers answer leading with shortening, ibuprofen while fasting).
items.why_flagged: FIX_HADI_REPORT and E_games_hadi list wrong-topic answers in a confident frame; the routing is the app's own.

items.where_in_app: Hadi > "Hadi checked this reply" and how-it-works text
items.what_to_review: The wording that says what Hadi checked and what a scholar has not.
items.why_flagged: Honesty copy; the "checked" claim must stay accurate.

items.where_in_app: Hadi optional AI tier (own key)
items.what_to_review: Any answer generated by an AI model with the user's own key is not from the built-in library and carries no review.
items.why_flagged: R9_T1 / R9_T4: "optionally your own AI key"; the Qur'an is never produced from memory.

items.why_flagged: OWNER_ACTIONS items 6 and 18: stores require a reachable privacy contact.

items.what_to_review: Data collection and deletion promises on the privacy screens.
items.why_flagged: OWNER_ACTIONS item 2: rules reviewed by reading, not executed.

items.what_to_review: The disclaimers about rulings and scholars.
items.why_flagged: Needs a lawyer to confirm the disclaimers are enough for store review.

items.where_in_app: What is free; ads and paid plan wording
items.what_to_review: Free and paid plan wording; ads.
items.why_flagged: R9_T2 / R9_T4 noted a "paid plan planned" line; confirm with a lawyer before billing.

items.where_in_app: Nasheeds / Player > verified catalogue (200 entries)
items.what_to_review: The "family-friendly" label for 200 verified nasheeds is a judgement from artist and title, not a scholar's review.
items.why_flagged: NASHEED_VERIFICATION_LOG: instrument use was NOT checked for entries marked unknown; target of 600 not reached.

items.where_in_app: Nasheeds > audio style (vocals / duff / music / unknown)
items.what_to_review: Whether a user who avoids instruments is served correctly by the vocals-only / duff / music / unknown classes. Scholars differ on music (the Q&A bank says so).
items.why_flagged: The app has no vocals-only guarantee; classes come from the uploader's own titles.

items.where_in_app: Nasheeds > official channel claims
items.what_to_review: Officialness of the uploading channels (labels, artist channels) for entries beyond Awakening Music.
items.why_flagged: Not independently corroborated beyond the artist/label name; the owner is asked to spot-check.

items.where_in_app: Nasheed lyrics and titles
items.what_to_review: Whether the lyrics of the listed nasheeds contain anything contrary to aqidah; titles were checked, lyrics were not heard.
items.why_flagged: Only title, channel and embeddability were fetched.

items.where_in_app: Recitation and Listen buttons
items.what_to_review: Recitation and Listen audio: which reciters are offered and the audio files themselves (stub or silent files were found in test).
items.why_flagged: R9_T1: Listen, recitation and speaker buttons UNVERIFIED; OWNER_ACTIONS audio CORS note.

items.where_in_app: Prayer Times > default method on first run
items.what_to_review: The method chosen automatically for a user who has not picked one.
items.why_flagged: FIX_WORSHIP_REPORT: verified maths, not the choice.

items.where_in_app: Prayer Times > "approximate, confirm locally"
items.what_to_review: The wording that says times are approximate and to confirm with the local mosque.
items.why_flagged: R9_T4 praised it; wording is the app's.

items.where_in_app: Need help now > "Not re-checked recently" help lines
items.what_to_review: Help lines marked unverified or not re-checked, and US-centric coverage outside the US.
items.why_flagged: B_worship audit; FACT_S4 re-verification dated 2026-10-20.

items.where_in_app: Hadi / Sakina > grief and child loss replies
items.what_to_review: Replies for bereavement, miscarriage and child loss.
items.why_flagged: Sensitive copy with no clinician or scholar review.

items.where_in_app: Health school; Hadi on fasting and medicine; ruqya
items.what_to_review: Health teaching (Prophetic medicine, dhikr and mental health, fasting and medicine, ibuprofen while fasting).
items.why_flagged: S2_eol_hlth_wmns_char: health content needs a clinician; Hadi refuses ibuprofen question with no doctor line (E_games_hadi #79).

items.where_in_app: Arabic and Urdu UI direction and font
items.what_to_review: Right-to-left layout and fonts for Arabic and Urdu; Bangla glyphs rendered as empty boxes in headless test.
items.why_flagged: R9_T4 D5, R9_T6_elder_languages: unverified on a real device.

items.where_in_app: Hadi > a reply to someone who talks about drinking, drugs, gambling, pornography, smoking or a relapse
items.what_to_review: Listening replies (three per topic), the safety note about not stopping heavy use suddenly, and the word lists that decide a person from a question.
items.why_flagged: RES_H3: a ruling card is the wrong answer to someone in relapse. Written for coverage; no clinician has read them. Shown with both "Scholar review needed" and "Clinician review needed" until signed.
items.label_surface: Under every support reply in Hadi

items.where_in_app: Hadi / Wasia > medical emergency card (overdose, withdrawal danger, mixing, drunk driving)
items.what_to_review: The new addiction and medical-emergency crisis category: English phrases, the card (emergency number first, no dose, no taper) and the follow-up checks after the card.
items.why_flagged: RES_H3 R5: no addiction or overdose category existed. Withdrawal from alcohol and sedatives can be fatal, so the wording must be read by a clinician.

items.where_in_app: Crisis phrases for the medical-emergency category in Arabic, Urdu (script and Roman) and Bangla
items.what_to_review: Short phrase lists for overdose, seizure and not breathing in Arabic, Urdu and Bangla.
items.why_flagged: Written for coverage, not read by a native-speaker clinician. English has the full list; other languages are thin and the app must say so.

items.where_in_app: Hadi / Wasia > the safety check after a crisis card ("ok", "tonight")
items.what_to_review: The plain questions asked when a short reply follows a crisis card, and the sentence said when the person says they are safe.
items.why_flagged: RES_H3 D1: follow-ups with no trigger word were treated as normal. The wording and the list of ambiguous words need a clinician.

items.where_in_app: Wasia and Kids > what a child is told when something is wrong
items.what_to_review: Replies now say "a trusted adult (a parent if it feels safe, a teacher, a school counsellor, or a child helpline)", that the child chooses, and that the app cannot call anyone.
items.why_flagged: RES_H3 R1, D5, D6: "tell a parent" can point a child at the person hurting them. A child-protection specialist and a clinician should read the wording by age band.
items.label_surface: Wasia thread, Kids Corner help button

items.where_in_app: Hadi > nothing about a conversation is saved; the API key leaves plain text; Report never uploads support text
items.what_to_review: The conversation is memory-only. The key is kept in the secure store on a phone and memory-only in a browser. Report drops text from crisis, support and minor exchanges.
items.why_flagged: RES_H3 D3, D4, D10: health disclosures were stored in plain text and could be uploaded by the Report button.
